svg.data-asic: Broadcom Qumran2c BCM88820 with optional Broadcom OP2 BCM16K external TCAM (premium SKU only)
svg.data-oem-alias: DriveNets NCP-64X8C-S (Network Cloud Packet forwarder, 64x1/10 + 8x100). NOT A UFISPACE CLAIM - no UfiSpace document mentions DriveNets. The mapping is internal analysis: the okf `drivenets-ddc` bundle's 'DriveNets NCF/NCP to white-box hardware map (shipping platforms)' matches the roadmap slide's NCP-64X8C-S (Q2C 2.4T) to this chassis on published silicon and port configuration. Recorded so a search for either name finds this box; no DriveNets figure or artwork is transcribed anywhere in this file.
svg.data-timing: Stratum 3E OCXO with optional holdover; SyncE (ITU-T); IEEE 1588v2 default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2 (additional licence), T-GM, T-BC/OC, T-TC; Time Sensitive Networking (TSN); Class C timing accuracy. NOS integration is required to activate these, which the datasheet states with an asterisk against the whole timing block
svg.data-gnss: internal receiver for master clock implementations
svg.data-compliance-programme: IEEE 802.1CM fronthaul; ITU-T G.8273.2 T-BC Class C
svg.data-roles: C-RAN hub 5G fronthaul transport aggregation; backhaul aggregation for BBU pooling; programmable as a Broadband Network Gateway (BNG)
svg.data-optics-qsfp28: 100G QSFP28 SR4/LR4/ER4/ZR4, up to 80 km per the HIG port table
svg.data-optics-sfp28: 25G SFP28 SR/LR/ER; 10G SFP+ SR/LR/ER; 1G SFP SX/LX/EX - the same cages take all three speeds, and the HIG's port table rates ports 0-63 to 40 km
svg.data-timing-cables: the datasheet's Compatible Timing Cable Types row - 50 ohm SMA coaxial with a 1/4-36UNS-2B connector for GNSS; 50 ohm SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector for 1PPS and 10MHz; shielded RJ45 for ToD. The accessory kit ships two SMB-to-BNC converter cables
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: 10G on the two SFP+ management ports. The datasheet's Compatible Transceiver Types list is one list for the whole box and names no management-only part, so the speed here is the port list's ('2 x 10G SFP+ management ports')
svg.data-timing-interfaces: GNSS SMA in; 1PPS SMB in/out; 10MHz SMB in/out; ToD RJ45 in/out
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 55024; EN 55035; EN 62479; EN 50663; EN 300 386; EN 301 489; EN 303 413; BSMI; MTCTE; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A

Built for 5G C-RAN fronthaul aggregation, BBU-pooling backhaul and BNG","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"HIG section 10 tables the five front-panel lamps, the PSU FRU lamp and the fan FRU lamp in full, and says nothing at all about the port lamps. So the eight four-lamp strips beside the QSFP28 block are drawn because the figure draws them, at a pitch that matches ufispace/lane-led-quad's own to a hundredth, but what the four dots mean - four lanes, link and activity pairs, something else - is not stated, and neither is which of the two rows in each strip belongs to which port of the pair. The binding written here (upper row to the upper port) is the natural reading and is an inference. Every lamp keeps the component's off/on default rather than a vocabulary borrowed from a sibling guide.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["qsfp28","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"THE 64 SFP28 LAMPS ARE THE TRIANGLES IN THE YELLOW BAND, and this gap used to say they did not exist. It said the hardware almost certainly had them, that HIG Figure 8's pale strip UNDER each module resolved to about two pixels at 9.585 px/mm, and that rather than invent 128 positions no reading supported, none were drawn. The search was in the wrong place: the lamps are above the modules, not below them, and the drawing already carried them - as 32 silkscreen marks reading `\u25b2\u25bc`, one per port pair, printed on the band. An up triangle for the top-row port and a down triangle for the bottom, which is the idiom the sibling S8901-54XC models correctly with common/led-arrow. Measured off the same figure, from the dark ink inside the yellow band rather than from a green cast beside it: each triangle is 2.35 x 1.47 mm, the two of a pair sit 2.79 mm apart, and the pairs repeat on a 14.37 mm pitch which is the port pitch. What remains unknown is only what they MEAN. HIG section 10 tables SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0 and PS1 in full and says nothing about any port lamp, so all 64 keep common/led-arrow-sm's own off/on default rather than a link/activity or speed vocabulary borrowed from a sibling guide.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["sfp28","port-leds"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace statement of what the S9600-72XC's port triangles indicate - link, activity, speed, or the pair together","what":"sfp28-port-led-semantics"},{"note":"The two-digit seven-segment display at x 411.8-429.0 is drawn in every figure and named in none. Figure 4's callout list ends at QSFP28 and section 10's Verifying System Operation covers the five panel lamps and the two FRU lamps only. Whether it shows a POST code, a chassis or stack ID, or a fault code is unstated, so the component carries no state vocabulary and its skin draws the all-segments '88' the vendor's own artwork draws.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["ufispace/seg7-status-2@1","display"],"wanted":"a NOS or BMC reference that documents the front-panel numeric display","what":"seg7-semantics"},{"note":"The HIG's Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 81 x 113 x 81.5 mm. This guide's own rear elevation puts the flat red airflow badge on an 84.3 mm pitch across the four modules, so the repeating unit is 84.3 and the visible face is that less a small web. The manifest carries the 82.5 mm face of ufispace/fan-803816@1 on an 84.3 mm pitch. Two library components claim this part number at two widths (82.5 and 80) and the three UfiSpace guides that describe it state three (81 here, 81 on the S9600-30DX, 80 on the S9600-28DX). The likely resolution is that the table measures the fan BODY behind a wider flange, which is an inference and which no document states.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ufispace/fan-803816@1","fans"],"wanted":"a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-803816-HI, or a caliper on the FRU","what":"fan-face-width"},{"note":"The only held view of the rear is HIG Figure 4's three-quarter render. Its face is 341 px tall at the left edge and 357 at the right, so there is no single vertical scale, and the right-hand third is magnified: the PSU's own drawn width exceeds the 50.5 mm its component table states. The fan bank is safe because it sits in the middle of the frame and its flat badges repeat, and it independently reproduces the S9600-30DX's 84.4 mm pitch. Everything to the right of x 340 - the grounding plate, the vent column, the PSU stack's left edge - is anchored on the latch position and is good to a few millimetres, not to a tenth, and the 13.3 mm of blank metal the manifest leaves right of the PSU stack is what that anchoring gives rather than something the figure shows.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["rear","psus","fans"],"wanted":"a dimensioned rear elevation, or an orthographic rear photograph","what":"rear-perspective"},{"note":"ufispace/psu-132-ac@1's provenance records a vendor convention that a supply built for front-to-back (intake) airflow carries a RED release latch and a back-to-front one BLUE, and that component draws the red-latched PSU-132-AISB1. This device's datasheet orders only the EXHAUST SKUs, PSU-132-AESR and PSU-132-DESR, and its own Figure 4 draws their latches RED. Either the colour convention does not hold across the range, or Figure 4 reuses the intake unit's art. The manifest seats the existing components and corrects the part numbers per configuration; it does not repaint the latch, because that would assert a colour on no better evidence than the figure it contradicts.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ufispace/psu-132-ac@1","ufispace/psu-132-dc@1","psus"],"wanted":"a photograph of a PSU-132-AESR, or a UfiSpace ordering guide that states the code","what":"psu-latch-colour"},{"note":"The HIG names the cord exactly - '250VAC 15A, IEC60320 C15' - and a C15 cord mates a C16 appliance inlet, not the C14 the modelled PSU composes. The library holds no std/c16; C14 and C16 differ by a notch below the earth pin and are the same 24 x 16 body, so at faceplate scale the drawing is right and the part reference is not. Recorded on the S9300-32D component too.","reason":"needs-hardware","scope":["ufispace/psu-132-ac@1","psus"],"wanted":"a std/c16-inlet component, or a close-up photograph of the PSU-132 inlet","what":"ac-inlet-standard"},{"note":"No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9600-72XC, and the Available to Order block names only the two PSUs and one fan. The datasheet's own footnote says 'OP2 available for premium SKU only' and its ASIC row lists the OP2 BCM16K as '(Premium)', so at least two SKUs exist and neither is named; the memory row's 'up to 64GB' implies another option with no part number either. The S9510-28DC precedent applies: that model's SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no held PDF, so the configurations carry no part numbers rather than invented ones.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["base","ac","dc"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace ordering guide, or the premium-TCAM and memory option SKUs","what":"chassis-sku"}],"groups":{"display":{"description":"the two-digit seven-segment readout at the right of the faceplate","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"Display"},"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"3+1","redundancy-note":"3+1 - the uplinks, and the only ports on this box the guide gives an 80 km reach for","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"sfp-plus":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp-plus","speed":"10g"},"description":"the stacked SFP+ pair at the left of the faceplate, numbered 0 and 1 in their own run on the panel's own '0 \u25b2\u25bc 1' legend - the datasheet's '2 x 10G SFP+ management ports'","index-origin":0,"role":"management","term":"Port"},"sfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp28","speed":"25g"},"description":"ports 0-63, the datasheet's '64 x 1/10/25G SFP28 ports' and the HIG port table's '0 ~ 63', in four ganged blocks of four columns. Numbering runs DOWN each column and the upper shell (0-31) is a separate run from the lower (32-63), so port 1 sits under port 0 and port 32 under neither","index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"status-leds":{"description":"the five chassis indicators the faceplate legends SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0 and PS1, each with a published state table in HIG section 10","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"timing":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the timing block across the top left - a GNSS antenna on SMA, 1PPS and 10MHz on SMB and ToD on RJ45. Note there is no BITS jack here, unlike the S9600-30DX","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9600-72XC","name":"s9600-72xc","portfolio":{"family":"Open Aggregation Router","line":"Telecoms","series":"S9600 Series"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"attrs":"datasheet - Specifications, Performance, Environmental, Regulatory Compliance and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied.","chassis":"datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 2 RU, 436 x 609.6 x 87.7 mm or 17.17\" x 24\" x 3.45\"', weight 15.19 kg without FRU. The HIG's Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple, but note that its Dimension row is LABELLED 'S9701-82DC (W x D x H)' - a copy-paste from another product's guide. The numbers are this product's (they match the datasheet and Figure 4's own dimension callouts, W = 17.17\" / 436 mm and D = 24\" / 609.6 mm); the label is not, and it is recorded here so nobody later reads it as a second source. That table gives the chassis weight as 15.06 kg against the datasheet's 15.19 kg, a 130 g difference recorded here rather than as a conflict - the manifest carries the datasheet figure. 436 is the body and not a rack face: Figure 4 dimensions 436 mm across the chassis itself and the guide ships separate adjustable mounting rails (626 x 44 x 22 mm) for 19 inch racks, so the mounting hardware is additional to 436 and is not drawn.","colour":"photo-measured - the faceplate samples #484848 in the 520 px product render and #474747 in the HIG figure, a neutral dark grey rather than the blue-grey (#3c3f42) the S9600-30DX carries. The yellow legend band samples #c2b339 and the QSFP28 light-pipe strips #4b6332.","fans":"datasheet/HIG - four FAN-803816-HI exhaust modules, 3+1 redundant. The HIG's component table gives the fan 81 x 113 x 81.5 mm, so the face is 81 x 81.5. The library holds two components for this part number, ufispace/fan-803816@1 at 82.5 mm (drawn for the S9600-30DX from an 84.4 mm bay pitch) and ufispace/fan-803816-hi@1 at 80 mm (drawn for the S9600-28DX, whose guide states 80). Neither is 81. The 82.5 part is used because the bay pitch measured HERE is 84.3 mm, the same repeating unit the 82.5 face was derived from, and a 80 mm face on an 84.3 mm pitch leaves a 4.3 mm seam the figure does not show. This is the third UfiSpace guide to state a fan width its own rear elevation contradicts and the likely resolution is the same one - the table measures the fan BODY behind a wider flange - but no document says so. See the fan-face-width gap.","grounding":"HIG section 8 - 'The location for securing the grounding lug is at the rear of the case and is covered with a protective label', with two M4 screws and washers and a #6 AWG lug from the accessory kit. Figure 4's rear elevation calls it out by name ('Ground Lug') with a leader to the silver plate between the fan bank and the PSU stack, and the plate is drawn there with two bolt bosses. Figures 20 and 21 show the lug fitted. The plate is drawn as decor at x 344.5-360.0 and the earth symbol is placed beside it.","left-cluster":"drawing - measured on the 600 dpi page at 9.585 px/mm and cross-read at 12x. Across the top, three round timing jacks with their legends to the left of each: GNSS ANT at x 21.70 (nut 9.81 mm), 10MHZ at 39.33 and 1PPS at 56.81 (nuts 7.72 mm), all on y 7.57. Below and left, a four-hex vent row, then the ToD RJ45 (aperture 8.35-21.07 x 30.84-41.27), a recessed reset pinhole at (14.7, 46.15), a triangular hex vent field, the five-lamp system LED legend block (white block x 15.13-19.51, y 66.52-76.33 with its lamp column at x 13.88 outside it) and the micro-USB console at the bottom. In the second column, the stacked SFP+ management pair (apertures x 27.13-39.96, centres y 21.61 and 35.59, a 13.98 mm pitch) over the out-of-band RJ45 (aperture y 49.8-60.3, two integral green lamps at its top corners), the USB 3.0 Type-A (aperture 23.27-36.10 x 62.14-67.67) and the RS-232 console RJ45 (aperture y 69.5-80.2). All three RJ45s are drawn CONTACTS UP AND LATCH DOWN - checked in a 12x crop of each, where the gold contact fingers sit along the top edge and the latch channel steps out of the bottom - which is std/rj45-ganged's own orientation, so none of them is rotated. std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11.0) is used rather than std/rj45 (16.0 x 14.0) because the measured apertures are 12.7-13.0 x 10.4-10.5 and a 16 mm part cannot sit in them.","lifecycle":"searched 2026-08-28 for 'UfiSpace S9600-72XC end of life end of sale announcement': the results are the live product page, the current datasheet, an FAQ and reseller listings, and no notice of any kind. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.","mirror":"drawing - the two shells MIRROR EACH OTHER, and the mirror is per SHELL rather than per row, which is not what the AGR400 lesson would predict and is therefore stated plainly. In HIG Figure 8 both rows of the upper shell draw their module latch tab at the BOTTOM of the cell and both rows of the lower shell draw it at the TOP. Rows 3 and 4 therefore carry rotate: 180 and rows 1 and 2 do not. std/sfp-ganged is very nearly symmetric about its own centre, so this changes little in the render; it is recorded because it is what the artwork says and because getting it backwards is invisible to every rule.","numbering":"drawing - NUMBERING RUNS DOWN EACH COLUMN AND THE TWO SHELLS ARE TWO RUNS. The top yellow band prints '0 \u25b2\u25bc 1', '2 \u25b2\u25bc 3' ... '30 \u25b2\u25bc 31' across sixteen columns and the bottom band prints '32 \u25b2\u25bc 33' ... '62 \u25b2\u25bc 63', so column k carries 2k over 2k+1 in the upper shell and 32+2k over 33+2k in the lower. HIG Figure 8's module faces print the same assignment stated the other way round (0 2 4 6 across the first row, 1 3 5 7 beneath), and the guide's Port Overview table agrees on the ranges: '0 ~ 63 SFP28 1/10/25G, 64 ~ 71 QSFP28 40/100G'. The band numerals are what is drawn here; the module-face numerals are on the schematic transceivers and would be covered by a real one.","power":"datasheet 'Typical power: 328 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. The HIG's AC connection step states the maximum once: 'Ensure there is enough power to supply the system. The maximum system power consumption is 685 watts', unqualified as to optics or ambient, and the DC section states no maximum at all. 685 is carried as power-max-w because a single unqualified figure on a provisioning instruction is what a chassis is budgeted with, AND THE VENDOR DID NOT QUALIFY IT. The 1300 W beside it is the supply's rating, not a draw. These are the vendor's figures as the vendor states them and are NOT reconciled against the module set; the fans publish no draw anywhere in the intake, so any total built from the modelled modules is a floor.","psu-inlet":"HIG - 'Attach the power cable. Locate the AC inlet connector on the PSU and plug the AC power cable (250VAC 15A, IEC60320 C15) into the AC inlet connector.' A C15 cord mates a C16 inlet, the notched high-temperature variant of the C14; ufispace/psu-132-ac@1 composes std/c14-inlet and records the same caveat, because the library holds no std/c16 and the two are indistinguishable at faceplate scale. Carried forward here as a gap rather than restated as fact.","psus":"datasheet/HIG - two 1300 W supplies, 1+1 hot-swap, ordered as PSU-132-AESR (AC, exhaust) or PSU-132-DESR (DC, exhaust). THE MODELLED COMPONENTS ARE THE INTAKE SIBLINGS. ufispace/psu-132-ac@1 and @1's DC pair were drawn for the S9300-32D as PSU-132-AISB1 and PSU-132-DISB1, and that component's own provenance records a vendor rule that intake supplies carry a red latch and back-to-front ones blue. This device's Figure 4 draws its PSUs with RED latches while its datasheet orders the exhaust SKUs, so either the rule does not hold or the figure is generic. The faces are otherwise the same 50.5 x 40 mm unit - the HIG's component table gives 50.5 x 321 x 39.9 mm here too, and its Figure 5 dimensions the AC body at 321 mm with 331.2 mm over the handle, the same drawing the S9300-32D guide carries. The part numbers are corrected per configuration through component-attrs; the latch colour is filed as a gap rather than repainted.","qsfp28-layout":"drawing - one ganged block, two columns by four rows, on the row grid above. Its white cage walls measure at 289.4/290.9 (outer and inner), 313.5 (shared) and 336.15 (right), so the two columns are 22.5 and 22.65 mm wide on a 22.58 mm pitch and std/qsfp28 (registry 20.0 x 10.15) is centred in each at 302.25 and 324.83. Numbering is column-major within each shell exactly as the SFP28 field: 64 over 65 and 66 over 67 in the upper shell, 68 over 69 and 70 over 71 in the lower, read off the module faces in Figure 8. NO PORT NUMERALS ARE PRINTED ON THE PANEL for these eight - the yellow legend band stops at 288 mm and the green light-pipe strips beside the block carry lamps and no digits - so none are drawn here. That is a statement about the artwork, checked at 12x, not an omission.","qsfp28-leds":"drawing - a green light-pipe strip runs above and below the QSFP28 block, each carrying two rows of four round lamps per column. The lamps' dark rings give centres at 295.25, 299.2, 303.2, 307.1 in the left column and 318.6, 322.5, 326.5, 330.6 in the right: a 3.95 mm pitch, which is ufispace/lane-led-quad's own 3.94 to a hundredth, so that part is reused rather than a new one drawn. The four rows sit at y 10.05 and 13.45 above the block and 74.0 and 77.4 below it. WHICH ROW SERVES WHICH PORT IS INFERRED, not stated: the upper strip is bound to the upper shell's two ports and the lower strip to the lower shell's, top row to the upper port of each pair. Nothing in the guide says so - see the port-led-semantics gap. A white diamond light-pipe closes the right end of each strip (x 310.8 and 334.1, spanning the strip's height); it is drawn as decor because no source says what it indicates.","rear-layout":"drawing, and WEAKER THAN THE FRONT - said plainly because the difference matters. HIG Figure 4's rear elevation is drawn in three-quarter perspective with the chassis top surface visible above the face, so the face is 341 px tall at its left edge and 357 px at its right; there is no single vertical scale. The horizontal scale is the face width (2500 to 4176 px = 436 mm, 3.844 px/mm) and on it the four fan modules repeat cleanly: the flat red airflow badge - chosen over the projecting handle, whose drawn width shrinks 43, 31, 23, 29 px across the frame exactly as a projecting feature must - sits on an 84.3 mm pitch with the first at x 16.1, putting fan bay 0 at x 1.55. THAT IS AN INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THE S9600-30DX, which measured 84.4 and 1.5 off its own guide's figure; the two devices share a chassis width, a height and a fan bank, and this reading was taken before that one was consulted. Vertically the bays are placed on the S9600-30DX's numbers, which this figure can neither confirm nor refute better than about a millimetre. The right-hand third of the face is magnified by the perspective and the PSU stack is therefore anchored on its left edge (the red latch at 372.8 less the component's own 0.6 latch inset) rather than on the chassis edge; see the rear-perspective gap.","row-grid":"drawing - THE SFP28 AND QSFP28 ROWS SIT ON ONE GRID, measured independently in two columns of the figure and agreeing. Profiling inside an SFP28 block gives the upper ganged shell running 16.95-43.45 mm with its shared cage wall at 30.2, and the lower shell 44.65-71.30 with its wall at 58.0: four cells of 13.28 mm. Profiling the QSFP28 block, 250 mm away on the same face, gives the identical numbers - shell top 16.95, wall 30.0-30.2, shell bottom 43.45, second shell 44.65-71.30, wall 58.0-58.6. The two blocks are therefore laid out on the same centrelines (23.58, 36.83, 51.33, 64.65) and each opening is centred in its cell.","scale-gate":"THE FIRST READING OF THIS FIGURE WAS 7% WRONG AND THE ERROR WAS CAUGHT BY AN IMPLAUSIBLE PITCH, so it is recorded rather than quietly fixed. HIG Figure 8's panel appeared to run from py 1668 to py 2567 on the 600 dpi page, which gives 10.262 px/mm and an SFP28 column pitch of 13.35 mm - smaller than SFF-8433's 14.25 mm ganged pitch, which is to say smaller than the part that has to fit in it. Re-reading the column showed py 2567 is the figure's own black RULE, three millimetres of white below the chassis; the chassis ends at py 2508.6. The corrected scale is 840.6 px / 87.7 mm = 9.585 px/mm, on which the same triangles measure 14.276 mm and the standard is recovered to two hundredths. Every number on the front and top faces is on the corrected scale. The figure passes Gate 1 by a CIRCULAR feature rather than by its outline, because the outline is clipped: the GNSS nut measures 9.81 x 9.81 mm and the two SMB nuts 7.72 x 7.72 and 7.72 x 7.72, so x and y scales are equal to the pixel. On that scale the right-hand clip is 5.4 mm, which is exactly the width of the 'S9600-72XC' legend the figure cuts through mid-glyph. The TOP view in HIG Figure 4 gates on its outline conventionally: 1211 x 1700 px against the stated 436 x 609.6 mm is 612.1 mm computed against 609.6 stated, 0.4% out.","seg7":"drawing - a two-digit seven-segment display sits at the right of the faceplate, bezel x 411.79-429.00 and y 8.41-17.90. The HIG never names it: Figure 4's callout list runs GNSS, 1PPS, 10MHz, SFP+, ToD, Mgt. Port, USB 3.0, System LED, Console Ports, QSFP, QSFP28 and stops, and section 10 tables the five panel lamps and the two FRU lamps and nothing else. It is modelled as a component (ufispace/seg7-status-2@1) rather than as decor because it is a part a person could put a number to, but it carries no state vocabulary - see the seg7-semantics gap.","sfp28-layout":"drawing - four ganged blocks of four columns, each column two ports high in each of the two shells, so 4 x 4 x 4 = 64. THE PITCH IS TAKEN FROM THE PRINTED TRIANGLES, not from the drawn module faces, because the triangles are flat artwork on the yellow legend band and repeat once per column. Their sixteen midpoints are 52.84, 67.03, 81.12, 95.41 | 114.09, 128.43, 142.72, 157.02 | 175.69, 190.04, 204.33, 218.57 | 237.45, 251.85, 266.09, 280.39, which is an in-block pitch of 14.276 mm (twelve intervals, spread 14.09 to 14.40) and a block-to-block step of 18.75 mm. 14.276 is SFF-8433's 14.25 port pitch to two hundredths, so std/sfp-ganged is placed on the standard's own 14.25 and the block origins are the measured ones; the residual against the triangles is under 0.3 mm anywhere in the row. The white cage walls corroborate: they fall at 42.29 and 45.22 (block 1 outer and inner), 165.6, 289.5 - the same four block boundaries the triangles imply.","sources":"UfiSpace S9600-72XC datasheet (working/intake/ufispace/converted/s9600-72xc-datasheet) for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, timing, power, environment, compliance and the FRU ordering lines; S9600-72XC Hardware Installation Guide (s9600-72xc-hig) for the overview and port figures, the accessory and component tables, the PSU and fan mechanical drawings, the LED tables and grounding. All front and top geometry is measured on the HIG's own pages re-rendered from the source PDF at 600 dpi (pdftocairo), not on the docling extracts, because the extracted figure is CROPPED at the page margin and its bounding box therefore cannot be aspect-gated. Three vendor product renders (photos/s9600-72xc-1-view, -2-view, -3-view) are 520 px wide and were used for colour and counts only. Checked for a vendor 3D model before trusting any figure, per the skill: the intake stages GLBs for ReadyLinks only and none for UfiSpace.","status-leds":"drawing/HIG - five lamps, not six, and the count is checked twice. The legend block at the lower left carries five rows against a column of five green lamps at x 13.88 on a 1.96 mm pitch from y 67.5 to 75.34, and HIG section 10's Front Panel LED table names exactly five - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 - in that order, with a full state vocabulary for each. There is NO ID beacon here, which is where this device differs from the S9600-30DX's six-lamp block. The legend text itself is illegible at the figure's own resolution; the row order is the table's.","timing-block":"drawing/datasheet - the datasheet is explicit that GNSS is SMA while 1PPS and 10MHz are SMB ('1 x GNSS input SMA, 1 x 10MHz input/output SMB, 1 x 1PPS input/output SMB'), and the drawn nuts agree in proportion: the GNSS nut is 9.81 mm across and the two SMB nuts 7.72. AND THERE IS NO BITS PORT ON THIS DEVICE - the sibling S9600-30DX has one on RJ48 and this one does not; the datasheet's Timing Interfaces block lists four lines and stops at ToD, and Figure 8 draws nothing in that position. The jacks are drawn as round bezels, so std/sma and std/smb sit on gold decor discs at the measured nut diameters rather than common/sma-jack, which draws a hex nut this hardware does not have - the same construction the S9311-64D, S9500-30XS and S9600-30DX needed.","vents":"drawing - hexagonal perforation. A band runs the width above the port field (x 44-406, y 0.5-10.8) and deepens to y 21.2 over the blank metal right of the QSFP28 block, and a second band runs below (x 44-430, y 76.2-87.2). The left cluster carries a four-hex row at y 15.5-20.8 and a triangular field at x 4.8-18.5, y 53.3-72.2 - drawn here as a RECTANGULAR vent patch, which is the only shape panel.decor has; the real field tapers to a point at its lower left and that is a simplification, recorded rather than hidden. Four of the hexes at x 388-402 in the upper right band read green in the figure, which is an internal PCB seen through the perforation rather than four lamps: they are not in any LED table, they are not aligned with anything, and no lamp is drawn there.","views":"Six views. TOP is the strongest face after the front: HIG Figure 4's footprint drawing passes the aspect gate at 0.4% and gives five long stadium recesses across the lid at y 122.4, 217.8, 312.5, 407.9 and 502.6 (pitch 95.1, each 23.4 mm deep and 406.5 mm across from x 15.0), plus three small bosses near the rear and a screw row along the front edge. Y = 0 IS THE REAR on that face, per the house convention and per the drawing itself, which prints the fan-module handles along its top edge. BOTTOM carries the compliance sticker at an estimated position - no held figure shows the underside. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT) carry the rail screws the HIG's rack-mounting section describes, at estimated positions; both side faces otherwise carry only symmetric content, so the depth-axis conventions are stated here rather than exposed by any asymmetric feature. circle.data-states: off ok standby fail input-lost warning
circle.data-description: HIG PSU FRU LED table - Off (no input power to all power supplies), Green (output on and OK), Blinking Green (standby state / only +5VSB on, or firmware updating), Red (critical event causing shutdown - failure, over current, short circuit, over voltage, fan failure, over temperature), Blinking Red (input power cord unplugged or input lost with a second supply still powered), Blinking between Green and Red (warning event, supply continues to operate - high temp, high power, high current, slow fan)
